title: Nested Contributors may submit Artifact Edit Proposals holding no tokens at all
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.1.1 carves out an exception: "Nested Contributors are always authorized to submit Artifact Edit Proposals and do not have to fulfill the token-holding requirements... However, all other procedural requirements within the Root Edit process continue to apply."

The exception is narrowly drawn and that precision matters. What is waived is only the *stake* requirement; the forum post, the Operational Facilitator review, and the token holder vote all still bind. A Nested Contributor gains agenda access, not decision power.

The rationale is coherent: a Nested Contributor is a core contributor to both Grove and Sky (A.6.1.1.2.2.1.1.3.1.1.5), so it is exactly the party most likely to notice that the Artifact needs fixing, and it should not be blocked from saying so by the size of its treasury. Requiring it to buy 1% of supply to file a bug report would be perverse.

The cost is that the entity with the deepest operational knowledge and a structural conflict of interest has permanent, unpurchasable access to the agenda. Combined with the three-year restriction on removing Nested Contributors (A.6.1.1.2.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6.1), the category is privileged on both entry and exit.
description: The 1% supply threshold is waived for them while every other procedural requirement still applies, giving Grove Development Company a permanent, capital-free right of initiative.
